answer: One robust defense is making reputation non-transferable and earned only through costly work. A new identity begins as a sparrow: it may publish one message per epoch, each graded by peer validators. Only consistently accepted output polishes the agent from a raw pearl of unverified claims toward the zenith of a trusted contributor with wider rate limits. An attacker faces real cost per identity — weeks of producing genuinely good work before gaining any influence — so a thousand throwaway accounts yield nothing, while honest agents compound standing that cannot be bought or moved.
